root_cause_clusters.RC1_INGRESS_BOUNDARY: Ingress adapters have compatibility escape hatches or insufficient immutable-identity validation, allowing package files, dependency URLs, or mutable container identities to bypass the intended source/digest boundary.
root_cause_clusters.RC2_SCANNER_FAIL_OPEN: Missing or unknown vulnerability evidence is converted into ALLOW and can be persisted as an ordinary decision instead of failing closed.
root_cause_clusters.RC3_CACHE_BINDING: Decision cache identity is based on user-facing artifact coordinates and TTL only, omitting immutable digest, policy generation, and scanner database generation.
root_cause_clusters.RC4_EXCEPTION_SCOPE: Exception lookup matches only artifact kind and name, ignoring digest, environment, and expiry.
root_cause_clusters.RC5_PERMIT_INTEGRITY: Authorization permits are unsigned compatibility strings and verification ignores expiry and current policy generation.
root_cause_clusters.RC6_AUDIT_DURABILITY: The audit writer intentionally drops deny decisions, so security evidence is incomplete across process invocations.

defects.observable_failure: A direct file: package source is admitted without being present in the trusted package-source set.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Blocking only apt/dnf wrapper names leaves the adapter escape hatch usable by local package installs.

defects.observable_failure: A direct HTTP(S) dependency URL is admitted even though the URL is not an approved dependency repository.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Checking vulnerability severity after download does not establish source trust for the artifact that entered the build.

defects.observable_failure: A container request with a non-empty but non-sha256 digest string passes the inherited immutable-identity guard.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Testing only for an empty digest still authorizes mutable or malformed container identities.

defects.observable_failure: When the scanner reports unavailable, the engine returns ALLOW instead of an enforcement denial.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Logging scanner outage while still returning zero leaves the host admission path fail-open.

defects.observable_failure: A digest absent from the vulnerability database is treated as ALLOW rather than unknown security evidence.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Treating an unknown digest as severity NONE makes missing data indistinguishable from a verified clean result.

defects.observable_failure: A fail-open scanner-unavailable ALLOW is eligible for the same persistent cache path as evidence-backed decisions.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Changing only the immediate outage response still leaves previously cached fail-open admissions reusable.

defects.observable_failure: An ALLOW created from an unknown scanner result can be cached and replayed without obtaining trustworthy evidence.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Fixing scanner lookup without invalidating unsafe cached decisions preserves the earlier bypass until TTL expiry.

defects.observable_failure: The cache key omits artifact digest and follows kind/name/version/source coordinates instead of immutable artifact identity.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Adding digest checks only for containers in the engine does not stop cache reuse under a mutable tag.

defects.observable_failure: A container tag that moves from a clean digest to a vulnerable digest can reuse the earlier cached ALLOW.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Scanning the first pull correctly is insufficient when the cache remains keyed by tag-level coordinates.

defects.observable_failure: Changing policy_version does not invalidate an otherwise unexpired cached decision.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Reading the new policy on every invocation does not matter if lookup returns a decision produced under the old generation.

defects.observable_failure: Changing scanner_db_version does not invalidate an otherwise unexpired cached decision.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Refreshing the vulnerability fixture cannot affect admission while the cache ignores the scanner generation.

defects.observable_failure: A cached DENY can remain authoritative after policy or scanner evidence changes because cache freshness is only TTL-based.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Special-casing cached ALLOW entries leaves stale denials and inconsistent operator behavior under the same storage contract.

defects.observable_failure: An expired vulnerability exception is still selected because lookup ignores the evaluation timestamp.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Deleting the single expired fixture does not enforce expiry for future waivers.

defects.observable_failure: A staging exception can authorize the same named artifact in production because environment is ignored.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Checking only artifact name and kind allows a valid lower-environment waiver to cross deployment boundaries.

defects.observable_failure: An exception for one immutable digest authorizes a different rebuilt digest with the same artifact name.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Version or name matching is not a substitute for binding the waiver to the scanned immutable artifact.

defects.observable_failure: ALLOW returns a permit whose payload is marked UNSIGNED and has no integrity protection.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Base64 or obscuring the payload would still allow offline mutation without an authenticating MAC/signature.

defects.observable_failure: Editing permit payload fields not used by the legacy verifier can leave the permit accepted.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Checking digest and instance alone does not prove the rest of the authorization claims were issued by PolicyGuard.

defects.observable_failure: A permit remains valid after its encoded expiry because verification ignores current time.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Issuing a short TTL has no security effect unless verification enforces it.

defects.observable_failure: A permit issued under an older policy generation verifies after the active policy generation changes.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Binding only artifact and instance allows authorization minted under obsolete policy to survive a policy rollout.

defects.observable_failure: DENY outcomes are returned to callers but omitted from audit.jsonl, leaving no durable record after the process exits.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Printing denial JSON to stdout does not provide append-only host evidence across separate process invocations.
